prompts.text: What do you want us to learn before either person makes a promise?
Which part of getting close feels worth taking slowly to you?
Attraction deserves honesty about readiness. What does readiness mean in your present life?
Tell me about a small interaction which changed how you saw a possible relationship.
Understand our differences early or enjoy discovering similarities before discussing differences?
We enjoy each other but imagine different next steps. What should we say plainly?
What would help you feel chosen without feeling hurried?
An exciting beginning leaves room for ordinary questions too. Which ordinary question matters to you?
How do you distinguish genuine interest from enjoying someone's attention?
Describe an early conversation which helped you relax your need to impress.
Which expectation would you rather discuss before it becomes a source of anxiety?
Our texting rhythm feels different from our in-person connection. What would you want to compare?
A slow reply is information about timing before it becomes a story about feelings. What would you ask?
What would make saying 'not yet' feel safe between us?
Hear how I handle disappointment or how I show enthusiasm?
Which parts of your independence do you want an early connection to respect?
Tell me about a time clear intentions made getting to know someone easier.
People sometimes plan a future before learning a person's present. What about your present deserves attention?
What do you want curiosity about your past to leave private for now?
One of us feels more certain sooner. How would we avoid turning certainty into pressure?
What does making space for a possible relationship require you to reconsider?
Chemistry need not settle compatibility. Which practical difference deserves honest discussion?
Describe a moment you realised you liked a person's character as well as their company.
Plan a thoughtful ordinary day together or discuss what an ordinary week would realistically allow?
What would you like me to understand about how you make important choices?

Which kind of affection would you prefer us to ask about rather than assume?

Tell me about a time someone respected your pace and became more interesting to you.
How would you like us to acknowledge uncertainty while continuing to get acquainted?

What helps you notice when excitement is making you overlook a genuine concern?
Discuss how we disagree or learn how we each ask for help?
An important difference appears after several good conversations. What would keep the discussion fair?
Describe a gesture which helped you feel considered without creating an obligation.
Which compliment would tell you I have been paying attention beyond appearances?
We might be drawn to qualities we do not yet understand. Which quality would you like to understand better in me?
What would make an honest lack of readiness easier to express?

What part of your weekly life would help me understand your availability fairly?
Tell me about an early expectation you now prefer to state directly.
Share why a relationship appeals to us now or discuss what we would not want to rush?
What does emotional steadiness look like during the uncertainty of getting acquainted?

Which part of feeling respected matters most before a relationship has a name?

Describe a conversation which made you interested in someone's way of thinking.
How do you want us to respond if our interest develops differently?

What does curiosity about your values look like without making you feel examined?

Tell me about learning an unexpected similarity through a disagreement.
Which part of yourself do you hope attraction does not distract me from noticing?
An honest beginning needs room for an answer neither person hoped to hear. What would make this possible?
What is worth knowing about how you protect time for people already in your life?

Learn how I spend time alone or how I make plans involving other people?
What would you like our conversations to reveal beyond whether we enjoy them?
Describe a time someone asked a thoughtful question instead of making a flattering assumption.
A possible relationship should fit real responsibilities, not only free evenings. What responsibilities shape your choices?

How do you recognise when you are agreeing because you like a person rather than an idea?
We both avoid mentioning a concern to preserve a good mood. How would we open the subject?
Tell me about an ordinary habit which increased your respect for someone you liked.
Discuss what commitment means or discuss how to recognise when we are ready to discuss commitment?
Which difference in communication would you prefer us to understand before judging it?

What would make you comfortable correcting a story I have formed about you?

How would you like us to talk about the influence of faith or values on dating?
Describe an early boundary which helped you feel more comfortable rather than less connected.
Hear what I value in your company or learn what I am still curious about?
What makes intentional interest different from constant contact for you?
Some people find labels reassuring; others need behaviour to give labels meaning. What helps you feel clear?
We realise our hopes involve different cities. Which questions deserve attention before imagining solutions?

Tell me about a time patience made someone's interest easier to trust.
What would you want me to ask before introducing you to people important to me?
Which kind of date leaves you enough room to notice how you feel afterwards?

Describe a moment you appreciated someone's honesty more than a smooth answer.

What would you want us to notice about how we each treat a person who has nothing to offer us?

What does taking someone seriously involve before making a commitment?

If a friend disliked me before meeting me, how would you want to handle their opinion?
What would you like a possible relationship to add without replacing what already matters?

Describe an interaction which made you notice how a person treats people's limits.

Learn how I handle uncertainty or learn how I respond when someone asks for space?

Which expectation about romance would you rather examine than inherit?
A special gesture feels bigger than the relationship currently feels. How would you acknowledge both kindness and discomfort?

Describe a conversation which made you appreciate someone's willingness to ask permission.
What helps you decide which differences invite learning and which require a harder conversation?

What would it mean to be considerate of the person waiting for clarity?

What would make discussing future hopes feel exploratory rather than contractual?

Tell me about an instance when realistic expectations made a connection more enjoyable.

How do you prefer someone to respond when you disagree with a romantic expectation?

Hear how I decide to trust or share how you recognise a connection worth exploring?

What should interest in your future never assume you owe somebody?

Tell me about an early conversation which helped you understand what you did not want to rush.
